# The Sea

The sea does not ask where you've been,
it only takes your footprints in.
Salt on the wind, a whispered hymn,
it calls to those who wander thin.

Beneath the waves, a world unspooled—
of silver fish and shadows cool,
of shipwrecks sleeping, deep and slow,
where only ancient currents go.

And when the dusk turns gold to gray,
it hushes all the noise away.

# The Sea

The sea does not ask where you've been,
it takes you as the tide takes in—
driftwood, salt, a broken shell,
all the things you cannot tell.

It keeps its counsel, deep and wide,
holding storms it cannot hide,
yet on the calmest, bluest day
it still remembers how to sway.

And when you leave, it does not grieve,
it simply writes you on its leaves—
